## Summary

3.5.0 no longer leaves a credential on a paid plan with a lower catalog when GitLab did not answer the tier detection, moves client-go from v3.30.0 to v3.49.0 and offers what that range models, takes `pagination` and `page_token` off the lists GitLab pages by offset alone, sends the empty value that clears a field where updates used to drop it, and answers a call the session cannot make with its cause on every surface.

- A tier detection GitLab did not finish no longer leaves a credential on the wrong catalog (#1816 to #1819). A step of the probe that got no answer (a timeout, a network failure, a `408`, a `429`, a redirect not followed or a `5xx` after the retries, or on GitLab.com a membership query answered without its group list) used to be read as an answer, so a credential on a paid plan could be served the Free catalog for hours, until its pool entry went away. Such a step now lowers nothing and leaves the tier provisional unless the steps that answered already reached `ultimate`: the highest tier the other steps answered is served, and a `WARN` names the steps. In HTTP mode the pool asks a provisional tier again about a minute after the build, then two, four and eight minutes after each ask, and every fifteen minutes after that, whatever `--revalidate-interval` says and whether or not the credential holds a subscription open, and moves the credential to the tier the answer resolves. The GitLab.com membership query is retried like a read and runs on eight seconds of its own, and an instance whose edition could not be read is no longer logged as CE. On stdio the tier is still detected once at start; a provisional one is warned about and kept until the client restarts the server.
- A call the session cannot make is answered with its cause (#1756, #1757, #1758). On the meta surface, an action the tier, the token's scopes or read-only mode withheld was refused as a value outside the `action` enum, which reads as a typo; it is now answered as the dynamic surface answers it, naming what withheld it. A param the session's tier leaves out of an action's schema is refused before anything is sent, on every surface, naming the tier it needs and whether the session's tier was pinned or detected, where the meta surface used to send it and GitLab dropped it. A session authenticated by an OAuth access token no longer lists the five actions GitLab refuses such a token on every route they send (`access.token_personal_revoke_self`, `access.token_personal_rotate_self`, `access.token_group_rotate_self`, `access.token_project_rotate_self` and `model_registry.download`), and a call to one is answered with that cause.
- client-go v3.49.0, reached through #1792, #1793, #1797 and #1798 and a last bump just before the cut, with #1794 offering the params the range models. The fields client-go now models are read from it, or kept from the captured response where its plain booleans would read an absent key as false, and three new actions build on the methods it adds: `group.group_upload` uploads a file to a group as `project.upload` does to a project (GitLab 19.0 and later), `group.shared_project_delete` removes from the group's side a share `project.share_with_group` created, and `environment.stop_stale` stops every environment last modified or deployed to before a time, protected environments excepted. Every tier serves three more actions.
- New parameters:
  - The merge request lists (`merge_request.list`, `merge_request.list_global`, `merge_request.list_group` and `environment.deployment_merge_requests`) filter by the merge user and the merge time, by `assignee_username`, and by seven negated filters (`not_assignee_id`, `not_assignee_username`, `not_author_id`, `not_milestone`, `not_my_reaction_emoji`, `not_reviewer_id` and `not_reviewer_username`); the global, group and deployment lists also by `environment`, `deployed_after` and `deployed_before`, the project list by `in` and the group list by `source_project_id` (#1794).
  - The five project lists take `topic_id`, `updated_after` and `updated_before` (#1797).
  - `admin.plan_limits_change` takes twenty-one more limits, `package.registry_get` asks for the repository's `size`, `user.create_service_account` and `user.update_service_account` take `external`, `project.update` takes the three GitLab Duo security workflow switches (Ultimate), and `group.group_board_create_list` creates an assignee, milestone or iteration column (Premium) as well as a label column (#1794).
  - `admin.topic_list` and `admin.topic_create` take `organization_id` (#1798), and the project and group hook add and edit take `url_variables` (#1792).
  - `pipeline.list` and `pipeline.latest` take the `canceling` and `waiting_for_callback` statuses, and a subscription to a pipeline, the latest pipeline or a job in either status is now polled as work in flight rather than as settled (#1798).
  - `user.contribution_events`, `user.get_status` and `user.ssh_keys_for_user` take a username as `user_id` (#1795), and the four custom attribute actions and the six storage move actions take a path or a username where GitLab does (#1745).
  - `package.download` takes `download_mode` (#1697).
  - `admin.terraform_state_lock` sends the lock info GitLab requires, so a lock now succeeds, publishes the lock GitLab recorded and names the lock already held on a 409, and `admin.terraform_state_unlock` takes a `lock_id` to release the lock only when its ID matches (#1796).
- Lists: only a list GitLab can page by keyset takes `pagination` and `page_token` (#1673, #1674, #1675): the four project lists, a project's issues and jobs, a runner's jobs, the user and service account lists, the three audit event lists, a container repository's tags, and the lists Gitaly pages. Every other list pages with `page` and `per_page` and refuses the two before sending anything (see Breaking changes). The four project lists refuse a keyset request in any order but `id`, which GitLab answered with 405.
- Updates send the empty value that clears a field (#1805, #1806, #1807). GitLab clears these fields with an empty string, an empty list or null, and the server used to read an empty value as the field left out, so nothing could clear them; the fields are listed under Breaking changes. `issue.update`, `issue.work_item_update` and `group.epic_update` remove a weight sent as null, and a weight of 0 is published where it used to be left out.
- Fixes:
  - `project.update` asks before it leaves a project's pull mirror overwriting diverged branches, as `project.pull_mirror_configure` has asked since 3.1.0, and both now also ask when a call sets the overwrite on a mirror it turns off, or changes the branch filter of a mirror that overwrites (#1753).
  - Inline comments: an image or file position is no longer refused as a text line, an image position of `x` or `y` 0 is sent, and a position missing its file path or a SHA, or a text position naming no line, is refused before any request, naming the part, where a draft note used to be saved and published as a general comment (#1700, #1760). `mr_review.draft_note_update` keeps the draft's position when it changes only the body, and its body when it changes only the position, and `repository.commit_discussion_create` runs the same checks.
  - `issue.list_all` and `issue.statistics_get` say GitLab.com may refuse `scope=all`, a restriction GitLab is rolling out per user, and answer that refusal with what works there; the `my_issues` prompt reads the caller's own issues with `scope=assigned_to_me`, and another user's from GitLab's GraphQL issue list when GitLab.com refuses `scope=all` (#1781).
  - A stdio start asks GitLab about the token, the user and the tier within ten seconds, where each question waited out its own timeouts and retries against an instance that accepts connections and never answers, and held a `tools/list` sent at start meanwhile (#1824).
  - A TLS failure on a host with no CA store names the store and `SSL_CERT_FILE` before turning verification off, in the startup warning and in the error a call returns (#1825).
  - In `oauth` mode, a client that registered itself with GitLab, which GitLab grants only the `mcp` scope, is refused with a pointer to the OAuth application's client ID rather than told to reauthorize (#1823).
  - `--probe` asks `/health` under a URL that ends in a slash, and refuses a scheme it does not speak with exit status 2 (#1826).
  - A stdio refusal whose request id cannot be read carries no `id` rather than `"id": null`, and the HTTP keep-alive comes 25 seconds after the last byte a stream wrote, where a stream could go 50 seconds without one (#1722).
  - The Markdown of every result writes an address that is its own text once, as `<url>`, and the user, topic and achievement cards leave the avatar to `structuredContent`, which still carries every field GitLab sent (#1724).
- HTTP mode and telemetry: every line the credential pool writes about an entry names the credential's keyed handle, so an operator can follow one credential from creation to removal without token material in the logs (#1755, by Kashif Manzer, and #1783). A fine-grained session whose grant was read logs at start what the grant decides (#1710). `gitlab_mcp.upstream.requests` counts every request the process sends GitLab, by server address and with telemetry off as well, against the per-address budget GitLab.com holds traffic to (#1706). Under `--telemetry-identity full` a caller is recorded with `gitlab_mcp.instance` beside its user id and name (#1707).
- Release and project: from this release, every release attaches its SLSA build provenance as `gitlab-mcp-server.intoto.jsonl` before it is published (#1682) and an OpenVEX document as `gitlab-mcp-server.openvex.json` (#1686), and CI refuses a dependency OSV.dev knows to be malicious or vulnerable (#1685). The binaries are built with Go 1.27.4 (#1800) and the image on Alpine 3.24.4; the release checks, the Claude Desktop bundle build and the plugin manifest check are Go commands (#1677 to #1679, #1719, #1720); and a winget submission that fails turns its job red (#1769 to #1771). The remote deployment guide's proxy blocks are now served by tests from the page and corrected where they failed, with a plain-HTTP block for a LAN (#1774 to #1777); the documentation site's deploy check requires the four security headers the site serves (#1669), and the site is linked by its root with a trailing slash (#1785); the license names the copyright holder as the source headers do (#1656); the Orbit live fixtures bring an existing project into line (#1735, by zgy); and the contributing guide lists the labels Dependabot applies (#1754, by Muhtasim Munif Fahim).

## Breaking changes

An empty value now clears these fields, where it used to be read as the field left out, so a call that sends one changes what it used to leave alone (#1806, #1807):

- An empty string or an empty list: the appearance's thirteen texts and colors; a broadcast message's color and font; the name of a system, group and project hook; a runner's description, maintenance note and tags; a pipeline trigger's description; a release's title and notes; a badge's name; a wiki page's content; a saved view's description; a feature flag user list's users; a group's default branch, step-up OAuth provider, IP ranges, allowed email domains and download limit lists; an approval rule's users, groups and protected branches; an external status check's protected branches; a push mirror's host keys and branch regex; a project's issue and merge request templates; a user's organization, profile texts and public email; the account-wide notification email; an environment's Flux path and Kubernetes namespace; the pull mirror's credentials and branch regex; the Jira and group Datadog integration texts; and the emoji and message of `user.set_status`.
- Null: a group and project member's expiry, and a package protection rule's two minimum access levels, which an empty value now sends as null.

Withdrawn, as the versioning policy allows in a minor release for what a tool could never honor:

- `pagination` and `page_token` on the 182 list actions whose routes GitLab pages by offset alone, which GitLab ignored or refused (#1674). The lists that keep them are named in the Summary.
- `order_by` and `sort` on `job.list` and `job.list_project`, which come newest first whatever is sent, and `include_retried` on `job.list_project`, which its route does not read (#1673).
- `order_by` and `sort` on `mr_review.changes_get`, `mr_review.diff_versions_list` and `issue.iteration_list_group`, whose routes read no order (#1674).
- `id` among the `order_by` values of `issue.list`, `issue.list_group` and `issue.list_all`, which none of their routes accepts (#1698).
- `url` on `admin.appearance_update`, and `notification_email` on `user.notification_group_update` and `user.notification_project_update`, which no route reads (#1806).
- A fraction in an image position's `x` or `y`, which GitLab truncated to an integer without a word: the coordinates take integers on `mr_review.discussion_create`, `mr_review.draft_note_create` and `mr_review.draft_note_update` (#1760).
- A project path as `project_id` on `job.token_scope_add_project`, `job.token_scope_remove_project`, `job.token_scope_add_group` and `job.token_scope_remove_group`, whose routes take the numeric ID alone and answered a path with 400. The schema now takes an integer, so the individual surface also refuses an ID sent as a string (#1731).

Refused before a request, where GitLab refused the call or did something other than it asked:

- A param the session's tier leaves out of the action's schema, which the meta surface sent and GitLab dropped (#1758).
- A keyset request to `project.list`, `project.list_forks`, `project.list_user_projects` or `project.list_user_starred` in any order but `id` (#1673), and `updated_after` or `updated_before` on `project.list` in any order but `updated_at` (#1797).
- `files` beside `content` on `snippet.create` and `snippet.project_create` (#1699).
- An inline position missing its file path or any of its three SHAs, a text position naming no line, a negative line, an image position on `repository.commit_discussion_create`, and a `mr_review.draft_note_update` naming neither a body nor a position (#1760).
- `group.group_board_create_list` naming none, or more than one, of a label, an assignee, a milestone and an iteration (#1794).
- A Pages domain's certificate or key emptied without the other, a `project.update` whose only setting is `mirror_branch_regex`, and an environment's Kubernetes namespace emptied while a Flux path remains (#1807).

Operators who read the logs or the telemetry (#1707, #1817):

- The log line `server pool: created new entry` carries a third `tier_source` value, `detected_provisional`, beside `configured` and `detected`, and then names the unanswered steps in `tier_unresolved`. A deployment that parses `tier_source` should accept it.
- `gitlab_mcp.credential_pool.eviction.reason` has a ninth value, `tier_resolved`, exported from start at zero like the other eight. It counts an entry moved to the tier a re-detection resolved: the entry's open `subscriptions/listen` streams end with `credential_reset` and the client reconnects, and under `--stateless=false` its sessions are answered `404` on their next request and the client starts a new one. A climbing figure says the tier detection keeps going unanswered at builds.
- Every pseudonymous telemetry digest changes once, the same person on the same instance included, because the digest now covers the instance as well as the user id, so two users with one id on two instances are no longer one caller.
- On GitLab.com the slowest entry build takes longer: when every step waits out its deadline, a new credential's first request now sends requests to GitLab for up to about 28 seconds once it holds a probe slot, against about 20 before (five for the credential probe, ten for the token, the license and the namespaces, eight for the membership query, and five for reading the user behind the credential). A self-managed instance has no membership step, and its worst build is unchanged. Counted from the moment the authentication gate admits the token, a build can first wait up to five seconds for that slot, and a fine-grained token up to five more for the slot its grant is read under, so on GitLab.com the first response can come about 33 seconds later, about 38 for a fine-grained token. In `oauth` mode the token is verified before that: up to five seconds waiting for a verification slot, then `GET /api/v4/user` and up to two introspections, ten seconds each, so the first response can come about 68 seconds after the request, about 73 for a fine-grained token.

## Upgrading

1. A proxy or balancer in front of HTTP mode waits for the first response to a credential it has not seen more than about 35 seconds in `legacy` mode, or about 40 to cover fine-grained tokens, and about 70 seconds in `oauth` mode, or about 75 to cover fine-grained tokens, or such a request may be cut before its entry is built.
2. A log pipeline or alert that reads `tier_source` accepts `detected_provisional`, a dashboard over the eviction reasons adds `tier_resolved`, and anything that joins telemetry on the pseudonymous digest expects every digest to change once.
3. Leave a field out of an update to keep its value: on the fields listed under Breaking changes an empty value now clears it.
4. Page a list that no longer takes `pagination` with `page` and `per_page`, and page the four project lists by keyset with `order_by=id`.
5. Leave a withdrawn parameter out of a call: the job lists come newest first, the merge request diff lists and the group iterations in GitLab's own order, and an issue list sorted by `id` takes `created_at` instead.
6. Send the job token allowlist writes the project's numeric ID, which `project.get` returns for a path, and an image position's `x` and `y` as integers.
7. Send `snippet.create` and `snippet.project_create` either `content` with its `file_name` or `files`, not both.
8. On a session served a lower tier than the instance is licensed for, pin the tier with `GITLAB_MCP_TIER` (or `--tier`); otherwise leave out the param a refusal names, which the instance's tier does not serve.

## Security

- Dependencies: Go 1.27.4 (#1800) fixes GO-2026-6859 (CVE-2026-97054), a race in `net/http` when the limit of `http.MaxBytesReader` is exceeded that can crash an HTTP/1 server, which the 3.4.0 binaries carry. HTTP mode wraps every request body in that reader, so its listener meets the advisory's precondition; the crash also needs a handler that reads the body while another goroutine sets a header, and the reads here happen on the request's own goroutine, so the exposure is narrow. stdio serves no HTTP. golang.org/x/crypto v0.59.0 no longer carries the `openpgp` packages GO-2026-5932 is about, which no release binary ever linked, so the OpenVEX document keeps its statement for the 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 images alone.
- In the release tooling and the documentation site, neither of which ships in an artifact: dnspython 2.9.2 in the lock the PyPI upload installs from fixes GHSA-vvf4-9x63-8xvv, GoReleaser 2.20.2 fixes GHSA-9422-8p9m-393x, which concerns publishing SSH keys this configuration does not use, and astro 7.4.12 fixes GHSA-mh32-jxcr-mh9f and GHSA-r3h5-4585-7x3w.
- Hardening without an advisory:
  - In HTTP mode, the state a multi-round elicitation hands its client between rounds was bound to its call and not to its caller, so state issued under one credential verified under any other credential of the same configuration shape for its ten minutes; it is now bound to the pool entry it was issued under (#1708).
  - In HTTP mode, a request the server could not attribute to a credential ran under one shared default state, so every such `tools/list` and `subscriptions/listen` drew on one rate-limit bucket and one listen counter; both are now refused and nothing is shared (#1709).
  - A GitLab-authored value such as an issue title written as `x](http://attacker.invalid/y)` held no `[`, so the Markdown escapers let it through and a renderer linked it to a host that is not GitLab; the escapers now break every literal autolink outside the addresses the server links on purpose (#1739).
  - Telemetry recorded no instance for a caller, so two users with one id on two instances shared one pseudonymous digest, while an exported log line carried the instance under every identity policy, `none` included; the instance is now part of the identity and follows its policy (#1707).
